chunks: Praise be to Allah, the Exalted

All praise is for Allah, the One whom senses cannot perceive, nor places contain, nor eyes see, nor veils cover. He is the One who indicates His eternity by the creation of His creatures, and by the creation of His creatures indicates His existence, and by their similarity indicates that there is no equal to Him. He is true in His promise, and is elevated above the injustice of His servants, and establishes equity among His creation, and is just in His judgment over them. He provides evidence through the creation of things of His eternity, and through what He marked them with of incapability regarding His power, and through what compelled them towards destruction regarding His permanence.

key_terms.حُدُوثِ خَلْقِهِۦ: The coming into existence of His creation

ai.seo_question: What are the key attributes of Allah described in the opening of Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: This passage from Imam Ali’s Sermon 1 in *Nahj al-Balagha* serves as a cornerstone of Shia theological discourse, articulating the doctrine of *Tawhid* through the lens of *Dalil al-Huduth* (argument from creation). It highlights the epistemological limit of human senses (*al-shawadhid* and *al-mashahid*) while establishing creation’s contingency as the primary proof of God’s eternal, uncreated nature (*al-Qidam*). This formulation underscores the Shia emphasis on rational theology (*Aql*) complementing revelation, affirming that divine justice and transcendence are logically deduced from the observable world's impermanence and dependence.

en.sayed-ali-raza: He is such that senses cannot perceive Him, place cannot contain Him, eyes cannot see Him and veils cannot cover Him. He proves His eternity by the coming into existence of His creation, and (also) by originating His creation (He proves) His existence, and by their (mutual) similarity He proves that there is nothing similar to Him. He is true in His promise. He is too high to be unjust to His creatures. He stands by equity among His creation and practices justice over them in His commands. He provides evidence through the creation of things of His being from ever, through their marks of incapability of His power, and through their powerlessness against death of His eternity.
